assessments.operationalization: Compare clutch size and broods per year of the common kestrel with other Accipitriformes and Falconiformes, and raptors as a group with other birds; the claim holds if raptors have low clutch sizes and the kestrel ranks at or near the top among them.

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: clutch size and clutches per year for raptors and other birds

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts of raptor breeding to fill gaps

obstacles: 'Unprolific' has no stated threshold, so the comparison group must be chosen.
Several small raptors (e.g. harriers, owls if counted as crooked-taloned) lay clutches as large as the kestrel's.
assessments.rationale: Clutch size is a standard, widely compiled trait, so both the group-level contrast and the kestrel's rank can be computed directly. The main interpretive step is deciding which birds count as 'crooked-taloned' and what counts as unprolific.

assessments.operationalization: Measure egg elongation and asymmetry and sex the embryo or chick; the claim is supported if elongated, pointed eggs are disproportionately female and rounded ones male, and refuted if shape does not predict sex.

candidate_datasets.name: Stoddard et al. 2017, Avian egg shape: form, function and evolution (Science)
candidate_datasets.role: egg shape measurements across birds, without offspring sex

obstacles: Open datasets pairing individual egg shape with chick sex are scattered across poultry studies.
Egg shape varies with hen age and laying sequence, which may confound any sex association.
assessments.rationale: The variables are clear and a sex-shape test is straightforward, but the data linking shape to embryo sex sit in individual poultry papers rather than an open compiled dataset, so only part of the claim (mainly in chickens) can be checked without compilation.

assessments.operationalization: Check whether females of the domestic hen and goose kept without males lay eggs; laying by never-mated females confirms the claim, and the absence of such laying refutes it.
obstacles: Evidence is in the poultry-science literature and production records rather than a single downloadable dataset.
assessments.rationale: Laying by unmated hens is the basis of commercial table-egg production and is thoroughly documented, so the observable part is effectively settled by existing records. Data existence is scored below the top because no single named open dataset is the obvious source.

assessments.operationalization: Mate hens sequentially with males of distinguishable breeds and assign paternity of chicks by plumage or genotype; the claim predicts the second male sires eggs mated before a developmental threshold, and that previously infertile eggs become fertile.
obstacles: 'Before the change of the yellow to the white' must be mapped onto a stage of follicle or oviduct development.
Sperm-competition studies in fowl report paternity shares, not the conversion of already-formed unfertilized eggs.
assessments.rationale: Sperm-competition and last-male precedence in domestic fowl are studied, which bears on the 'change of breed' part, but the specific claim that a formed wind-egg becomes fertile needs interpretation and data are scattered across papers.

assessments.operationalization: Compare incubation durations of chicken eggs under broody hens in warm versus cold seasons, or as a function of incubation temperature; the claim is confirmed if summer clutches hatch near 18 days and winter clutches take up to about 25.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: typical incubation period for Gallus gallus

obstacles: Natural-brooding records across seasons are scattered; most data come from artificial incubators at controlled temperatures.
The typical figure is about 21 days, so the stated range must be tested against variance, not just the mean.
assessments.rationale: The direction of the effect (cooler, longer) is testable from incubation-temperature studies, and the mean hatch time is standard, but season-specific durations under brooding hens would have to be compiled from scattered sources.

assessments.operationalization: Regress incubation period on adult body mass across bird species, with phylogenetic correction; a positive scaling confirms the claim, no relation refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: incubation period and adult body mass for thousands of bird species

candidate_datasets.name: AVONET
candidate_datasets.role: body mass and taxonomy for nearly all bird species

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: incubation period and body mass cross-check

obstacles: Phylogenetic non-independence and life-history mode (altricial versus precocial) must be controlled.
assessments.rationale: Both variables are in open trait databases with broad coverage, and allometric regression is routine. Confounding by developmental mode lowers discriminating power slightly but does not prevent a clear test.

assessments.operationalization: Use the standard chick staging series to find when the embryo first becomes visible and whether the beating heart is the first organ visible to the eye; agreement on timing and order confirms the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Hamburger and Hamilton 1951, A series of normal stages in the development of the chick embryo
candidate_datasets.role: timed stage descriptions including onset of heartbeat

obstacles: 'First indication' and 'first' organ depend on naked-eye observation, whereas staging tables record structures visible under magnification.
The scaling with larger and smaller birds requires comparative staging data that are scattered.
assessments.rationale: The hen part can be checked against a canonical staging series, but the claim is about what is first visible to the unaided eye, which needs interpretation, and the comparative part across bird sizes is not compiled.

assessments.operationalization: Measure relative head and eye size versus trunk across embryonic stages of birds and fishes and track yolk volume; the claim holds if anterior structures are proportionally largest early and yolk is progressively absorbed.

candidate_datasets.name: Hamburger and Hamilton 1951 chick staging series
candidate_datasets.role: chick embryo morphology through development

candidate_datasets.name: Kimmel et al. 1995, Stages of embryonic development of the zebrafish
candidate_datasets.role: fish embryo morphology and yolk absorption

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: zebrafish anatomy and stage ontology

obstacles: 'Upper part of the egg' and 'largest' need interpretation (absolute versus relative size).
Two model species stand in for all birds and fishes.
assessments.rationale: Staging series show the anterior-first pattern qualitatively, but quantitative relative-size data are not compiled across many taxa, and the claim bundles several observations that each need operational choices.

assessments.operationalization: Molecularly sex both eggs of two-egg pigeon clutches, recording laying order; the claim predicts mixed-sex clutches far above the binomial expectation of 50% and a male-first bias.
obstacles: Sex-by-laying-order data for Columba livia are in individual papers, not an open compiled dataset.
Sample sizes in published studies may be small.
assessments.rationale: The test is clean once clutch-level sex data exist, since the binomial null is explicit. Such data exist in scattered studies of pigeons and doves, so the claim is checkable only after compilation.

assessments.operationalization: Compile clutch size, number hatched and number fledged for eagle species, and the observed cause of loss of the younger chick; the claim is confirmed if broods are routinely reduced to one and the mother removes the chick, and contradicted if loss is through sibling aggression or starvation without maternal ejection.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: clutch and brood size accounts for eagle species

obstacles: 'Eagle' maps to several Aquila and Haliaeetus species with different brood-reduction patterns.
Behavioural observations of how the chick dies are in field studies, not trait databases.
assessments.rationale: Clutch and fledging numbers are compiled, but the distinctive part, maternal ejection versus siblicide, needs nest-observation literature, which is scattered and species-specific.

assessments.operationalization: Check that the common cuckoo builds no nest, count cuckoo eggs per parasitized nest, record whether the female removes or eats host eggs when laying, and compare host size with cuckoo size.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: breeding behaviour of Cuculus canorus

obstacles: Host-egg removal and eggs-per-nest data come from field studies rather than a single open dataset.
The stated preference for the ringdove nest conflicts with known host lists and needs a host-record source.
assessments.rationale: Brood parasitism in the cuckoo is very well studied, so each component is checkable, but the quantitative parts (eggs per nest, egg removal, host preferences) must be compiled from field literature.

assessments.operationalization: Compare testis mass in breeding versus non-breeding seasons across bird species, and test whether the seasonal increase is larger in species with higher copulation frequency or more polygynous mating.
obstacles: 'More salacious' must be proxied (copulation rate, mating system, sperm competition).
Seasonal testis-mass data are in scattered comparative papers.
assessments.rationale: Seasonal testis recrudescence in birds is well documented, so the first part is easy to confirm; the comparative part needs a proxy for salaciousness and compilation of testis data.

assessments.operationalization: Determine whether nestling swallows whose eyes are destroyed regain vision; recovery of sight confirms, permanent blindness refutes.
obstacles: No dataset records outcomes of such injuries in swallows.
The experiment would be ethically unacceptable; only incidental injury or regeneration studies in other birds could bear on it.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is concrete, but no existing data address it for swallows, and what 'prick out' means (corneal injury versus enucleation) changes the expected outcome.

assessments.operationalization: Tabulate reproductive mode across chondrichthyans and bony fishes; the claim is refuted if a substantial share of cartilaginous fishes are oviparous, or if many bony fishes bear live young, and the fishing-frog's mode is checked separately.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive guild and mode for sharks, rays and bony fishes

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic placement of the fishing-frog (anglerfish) relative to chondrichthyans

obstacles: Reproductive mode is missing for many species in FishBase.
The fishing-frog is a bony fish, so its 'exception' status depends on accepting Aristotle's grouping.
assessments.rationale: Reproductive mode is a recorded trait and the claim makes an all-or-none statement, so oviparous skates and catsharks, and live-bearing teleosts, would discriminate cleanly against it.

assessments.operationalization: Check whether embryos of Mediterranean Mustelus species are connected to the uterine wall by a yolk-sac placenta after the yolk is used up; presence confirms, a purely yolk-dependent (aplacental) development refutes.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproduction notes for Mustelus mustelus and congeners

obstacles: The 'smooth shark' may map to Mustelus mustelus (placental) or Mustelus asterias (aplacental), which give opposite answers.
assessments.rationale: Placental viviparity in Mustelus is described in the reproductive literature, giving a clear-cut test, but the result depends on which smooth-hound Aristotle meant.

assessments.operationalization: Test whether guitarfishes are hybrids of angel sharks and skates by their phylogenetic position, and whether natural interspecific hybrids are rare among fishes; a guitarfish lineage separate from both, and documented natural fish hybrids, would refute the respective parts.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Tree of Life
candidate_datasets.role: phylogenetic placement of Rhinobatidae, Squatinidae and Rajidae

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomy and records of hybrid fishes

obstacles: 'Variety' of fish is vague: hybridization frequency depends on whether close congeners count.
No single dataset counts natural fish hybrids.
assessments.rationale: The rhinobatus-as-hybrid part is cleanly testable from phylogeny; the general no-hybridization rule needs an operational definition of 'variety' and compilation of hybridization records.

assessments.operationalization: Check reproductive mode for all cetacean species; a single oviparous cetacean would refute the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: gestation length and litter size for cetacean species

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: gestation and life-history records for cetaceans

assessments.rationale: Cetaceans map unambiguously to a modern clade and live birth is recorded for every studied species, so the test is direct and trivial to run.

assessments.operationalization: Compare recorded maximum longevity of Mediterranean delphinids with the stated 25 to 30 years; the claim is confirmed if individuals routinely exceed 25 years.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: maximum longevity of Delphinus delphis and Tursiops truncatus

obstacles: The 'dolphin' could be the common or the bottlenose dolphin, which differ in longevity.
'Some exceed 25 years' is a weak claim compatible with a wide range of lifespans.
assessments.rationale: Maximum longevity is recorded in open databases and photo-identification studies, but the claim is a lower bound on some individuals, which limits how sharply it can be refuted.

assessments.operationalization: Map the erythrinus and channa to modern species and check whether captured individuals always carry ripe ova and whether separate males are absent, as in simultaneous hermaphrodites.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: sexuality and reproduction records for candidate Serranus and Pagellus species

obstacles: The names map uncertainly (Serranus cabrilla, Serranus scriba, or Pagellus erythrinus), with different reproductive systems.
'Pregnant' must be read as carrying ripe ovaries.
assessments.rationale: If the mapping to simultaneously hermaphroditic serranids is accepted, published gonad data can test the observation, but the mapping is uncertain and alternative identifications give different answers.

assessments.operationalization: Compare development of externally spawned eggs with and without exposure to milt; development only in milt-exposed eggs confirms the claim.
obstacles: Fertilization data are spread across aquaculture and reproductive-biology papers.
The extension to cuttlefish, which fertilize internally, needs separate treatment.
assessments.rationale: External fertilization is thoroughly established in fish, and controlled fertilization trials discriminate cleanly, but the evidence is in experimental literature rather than an open dataset, and the cephalopod scope does not fit the same test.

assessments.operationalization: Test whether most marine fishes spawn nearshore, and whether nearshore spawning sites are warmer, richer in food and lower in egg predation than offshore alternatives.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: spawning ground and habitat descriptions

obstacles: Many pelagic species spawn offshore, so 'fish in general' needs a defined species set.
The explanatory part (warmth, food, protection) is confounded; these factors covary and are hard to separate.
assessments.rationale: The descriptive part (where fish spawn) is partly checkable from spawning-habitat records, but the three-part causal explanation cannot be cleanly distinguished from rival explanations with existing data.

assessments.operationalization: Examine the ventral brood structure of Mediterranean pipefishes: whether the eggs leave through a split that closes again, and which sex carries the eggs.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive notes for Syngnathus species

obstacles: Aristotle attributes the structure to the spawning fish, while in pipefishes the male broods, so the claim's subject must be interpreted.
Pouch anatomy data are in morphological papers rather than open datasets.
assessments.rationale: The anatomy of syngnathid brood pouches is described in the literature and could confirm the opening and closing, but which individual is meant and what counts as 'bursting' need interpretation.

assessments.operationalization: Compare the duration of male nest guarding and egg development time in Silurus aristotelis with the stated 40 to 50 days, and with other freshwater fishes.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: species account and reproduction records for Silurus aristotelis

obstacles: Field data on guarding duration in this endemic Greek catfish are limited to a few studies.
assessments.rationale: The mapping to Silurus aristotelis is widely accepted and paternal care is documented, giving a direct quantitative check, but guarding-duration data are sparse and not in a compiled dataset.

assessments.operationalization: Test the observable consequences: whether eels possess gonads and gametes, and whether juvenile eels derive from eggs and larvae rather than from worm-like growths in mud; documented ovaries, testes and leptocephalus larvae would refute the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: life cycle and reproduction of Anguilla anguilla

obstacles: Eel gonads mature only during the oceanic migration, which is why they are rarely seen in fresh water; the test must use migrating or hormonally matured eels.
assessments.rationale: The spontaneous-generation mechanism makes observable predictions (no gonads, no eggs or larvae) that the eel life-cycle literature directly contradicts, giving a clean test even though the data are in published studies.

assessments.operationalization: Look up the migratory category of Anguilla and Mediterranean Mugilidae; the claim holds if eels are catadromous (moving seaward to breed) and grey mullets move from the sea into fresh and brackish water.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: migration category (catadromous, amphidromous) for eels and mullets

obstacles: 'Mullet' covers several Mugilidae species with differing freshwater use.
assessments.rationale: Migration category is a standard recorded trait for both groups, so the directional contrast can be checked directly; the mullet species mapping adds minor uncertainty.

assessments.operationalization: Test the observable consequence: whether fish appearing in refilled ponds and in sandy shallows derive from eggs, larvae or immigrants, using studies of fish colonisation of temporary waters and of the larvae of small clupeoids and gobies.
obstacles: The fishes Aristotle had in mind (Cnidos mullet, 'froth' fry) are not identifiable with confidence.
Recolonisation studies cover particular systems, not the localities he describes.
assessments.rationale: The modern answer (eggs, diapause stages or immigration) is well supported in general, but tying it to his specific cases requires interpretation, and data are scattered across studies of temporary waters.

assessments.operationalization: Compile egg incubation or gestation durations in days for many fish species and test whether they cluster on multiples of seven more than expected by chance; a uniform distribution of remainders refutes the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: egg development and reproduction records

obstacles: Durations depend strongly on temperature, so a single number per species is ill-defined.
'Gestation' in oviparous fish must be interpreted (time from fertilization to hatching, or carrying of roe).
assessments.rationale: Duration data exist for many species and the multiple-of-seven test is simple, but the definition of gestation and temperature dependence make any single-value test fragile.

assessments.operationalization: Compare fecundity and size at birth or hatching between chondrichthyans and bony fishes, and between viviparous and oviparous chondrichthyans; lower fecundity and larger offspring in viviparous forms support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fecundity, length at birth and reproductive mode

obstacles: Oviparous sharks and skates also have low fecundity, so viviparity and cartilaginous status are confounded.
Juvenile survival is rarely measured.
assessments.rationale: Fecundity and offspring size are recorded for many species, so the comparative pattern is easy to test; the causal 'because viviparous' and the survival component are harder to isolate.

assessments.operationalization: For a set of mammals, compare rates of male aggression in the mating season with other seasons, and female aggression shortly after birth with other periods; peaks in those periods support the claim.
obstacles: Aggression is measured differently across behavioural studies and is not compiled in any trait database.
'Animals' is unbounded; the test would cover a chosen subset of mammals.
assessments.rationale: Seasonal male aggression and maternal aggression are documented in many individual studies, so a restricted-scope test is possible, but harmonizing behavioural measures would take substantial compilation.

assessments.operationalization: Combine mating season and gestation length to predict birth timing across mammals, and test whether births coincide with seasonal food peaks more than expected; also test whether mating is concentrated in spring.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: gestation length and life-history traits for mammals

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: breeding season descriptions

obstacles: Breeding seasons are mostly in text accounts and must be coded.
The adaptive explanation is hard to separate from rival explanations of birth timing such as photoperiod constraints.
assessments.rationale: The descriptive parts are testable after coding breeding seasons, but the 'adapted so as to' part is a functional explanation whose test relies on a proxy (birth timing versus food peaks) with confounds.

assessments.operationalization: Compare recorded gestation length, litter size and lifespan of domestic sheep and goats with five months, usually two lambs, eight and ten years.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: gestation length, litter size and longevity for Ovis aries and Capra hircus

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: life-history traits for wild Ovis and Capra

obstacles: Lifespan of domestic animals depends on husbandry and culling; ancient breeds differed from modern ones.
assessments.rationale: Each stated value maps directly onto a standard life-history variable available in open databases, so a numeric comparison is immediate.

assessments.operationalization: Link mating dates of ewes and does to wind direction on those days and test for a difference in offspring sex ratio between north-wind and south-wind matings.
obstacles: No open dataset combines individual mating dates, offspring sex and local wind direction.
Wind direction covaries with season and weather, confounding any association.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is clear and testable in principle, but the needed linkage of flock breeding records to wind data does not exist publicly and would need new data collection.

assessments.operationalization: Check which deciduous teeth dogs shed and at what age; shedding of incisors and premolars as well as canines refutes the claim.
obstacles: The evidence is in veterinary dental references rather than a downloadable dataset.
assessments.rationale: Canine tooth replacement is standard veterinary knowledge with an unambiguous answer, so the claim is decidable immediately despite the lack of a single named open dataset.

assessments.operationalization: Compare lifespan of male and female horses, of breeding stallions versus geldings or non-breeding males, and of stabled versus herd-kept horses; shorter lives in breeding males support the claim.
obstacles: Horse longevity records are held in breed registries and insurance data that are mostly not open.
Husbandry, use and culling confound both the sex and the stabling comparisons.
assessments.rationale: The sex difference in lifespan could be checked with registry data, but the causal attribution to sexual service is confounded and open data are limited.

assessments.operationalization: Compare body size and conformation of mules (mare mother) and hinnies (jenny mother) with each parent species; the claim predicts mules closer to horses and hinnies closer to asses.
obstacles: Morphometric data on mules versus hinnies are few and scattered.
'Looks' and 'vigour' need operational definitions.
assessments.rationale: The reciprocal-cross comparison is a clean design, but morphometric data for hinnies are sparse, and only size can be measured straightforwardly.

assessments.operationalization: Compute neonate mass divided by maternal mass across species and check whether bears have the lowest ratio; any species with a smaller ratio (e.g. marsupials) refutes the 'of all animals' form.

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: neonate body mass and adult body mass for mammals

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: birth or hatching mass and adult mass across amniotes

obstacles: 'All animals' includes egg-laying and marsupial taxa, where the comparison of newborn size needs care.
assessments.rationale: Both masses are standard compiled variables, the ratio is trivial to compute, and the superlative claim is directly refutable by any lower ratio.

assessments.operationalization: Compare published external genital anatomy of male and female hyenas with the described arrangement: males with a penis and a blind pouch-like structure, females with a separate true vulva.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts of Hyaena hyaena and Crocuta crocuta anatomy

obstacles: The striped hyena and the spotted hyena differ greatly in female genital anatomy, so the answer depends on the species mapping.
Detailed anatomical descriptions are in specialist papers.
assessments.rationale: The negative claim (not hermaphrodites) is easily confirmed, but the specific anatomical description needs the right species and specialist literature.

assessments.operationalization: Check breeding-season length, litters per year and documented superfetation in European hares; year-round breeding, monthly litters and superfetation confirm the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: litters per year and reproductive traits for Lepus europaeus

obstacles: Superfetation evidence comes from specialised reproductive studies, not trait databases.
Breeding season varies with latitude.
assessments.rationale: Litters per year is compiled, and superfetation in hares is reported in the reproductive literature, so the claim is checkable in parts, but year-round monthly breeding needs regional data.

assessments.operationalization: Across mammals, test whether gestation length and growth rate predict maximum lifespan, and where deer fall relative to the trend.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: maximum longevity, gestation length and growth parameters

candidate_datasets.name: PanTHERIA
candidate_datasets.role: gestation length and body mass for mammals

obstacles: Body size drives both gestation length and lifespan, so the relation must be tested with size controlled.
The claim is an inference rule rather than a precise numeric prediction.
assessments.rationale: The variables are in open databases with broad coverage and the analysis is routine, but size confounding limits how clearly the result can be attributed to gestation and growth rather than body mass.

assessments.operationalization: Use long-term rodent population series with rainfall and predator data to test whether outbreak declines follow heavy rain and whether predation fails to curb peak densities.

candidate_datasets.name: BioTIME
candidate_datasets.role: assemblage time series that include some rodent populations

obstacles: Rodent outbreak series are mostly from particular regions and species not matching Aristotle's.
Rainfall also triggers outbreaks through food supply, so the direction of the rain effect is confounded.
assessments.rationale: Outbreak dynamics are studied with time series, so parts of the claim can be examined, but data are regional and the rain-decline link is confounded with rain-driven outbreak onset.
